Thank you for the valuable comments regarding our manuscript. We have taken all suggestions into consideration and updated the paper to reflect these improvements. Please find our detailed responses to each point below

How did you check the defects in the specimen? Please clarify.

Response: The surfaces of all samples from each group were examined after separation by a trained assessor who was unaware of the sample groups, using an SKT 41322 MEIJI TECHNO dissecting microscope. The failure modes were classified according to ISO 10365:2022 E.

The failure percentage was determined as follows:

A failure was classified as adhesive when approximately 25% of the cement remained on the fractured surface, cohesive when approximately 75% remained, and mixed when the remaining cement percentage fell between these two values.

 

How did you control the bonding area? Please clarify.

Response: Circular adhesive sheets were fabricated and precisely punched using a specialized tool to create a defined 3 mm diameter hole. The sheets were then applied to the zirconia surfaces to standardize the working area.

 

How did you control the film thickness of resin cement? Please clarify.

Response: A constant pressure of 5 kg was applied to the samples using a pressure-standardizing device in order to ensure uniform cement thickness and standardize the testing conditions. The device was located in the Department of Fixed Prosthodontics, Faculty of Dentistry, University of Damascus.

 

Please clarify and fill in deep detail for this sentence: "Cementation was performed under a constant load using a standardized metal device."

Response: The term "constant load" refers to the pressure-standardizing device mentioned in the previous section.

 

Please clarify the blade in the SBS test (notch-edge or knife blade) and the reason you use the blade.

Response: The blade used in the shear test was a chisel-edge blade, as the chisel method is considered more practical, faster, and easier to handle during testing. This method is recommended by ISO/TS 11405:2003 and has been adopted in numerous previous studies (Baiomy et al 2023) and these are references (1) in the article.

Please clarify the details of SEM.

 Response: The aluminum holder of the electron microscope was mounted on the plastic base, and double-sided carbon adhesive tape was applied to the holder. The sample was then placed with the zirconia surface facing upward. The aluminum holder with the sample was transferred to the examination stage using tweezers, and the microscope chamber was closed.

Please answer the hypothesis in the discussion section.

 Response: A paragraph has been added to the Discussion section addressing whether the results support the initial hypothesis.

The study hypothesis was partially rejected. While significant differences were observed between Group 3 and the other two groups (Groups 1 and 2) regarding both surface roughness and shear bond strength (p < 0.001), no statistically significant differences were found between Group 1 and Group 2 (p > 0.05). Consequently, the hypothesis that all groups would differ significantly from one another was only partially supported.

 

Please add the clinical application.

Response: Clinical Application

A paragraph has been added to emphasize the clinical relevance of the findings, highlighting their importance in improving bonding between ceramic and zirconia in dental applications.

"Heat-induced maturation and selective infiltration etching produced a reliable and profound zirconia-resin bond strength resistant to artificial aging, thereby enhancing the long-term clinical longevity of the restorations. Furthermore, these findings support the clinical feasibility of using translucent zirconia veneers as a durable and aesthetic restorative option."

 

Please rewrite the conclusion.

Response: The Conclusion has been rephrased to clearly summarize the main findings and provide practical recommendations.

Conclusions

In this in-vitro study, SIE proved to be more effective than conventional air-abrasion and CoJet systems for modifying translucent zirconia surfaces. SIE-treated specimens showed the highest shear bond strength and mainly cohesive failures, indicating a strong and durable zirconia-resin interface. SEM analysis revealed a honeycomb-like nanoporous structure that enhanced resin infiltration, whereas sandblasted and CoJet surfaces exhibited irregular grooves and loosely attached silica clusters, resulting in lower retention. The superior adhesion with SIE is attributed to its three-dimensional nanoporous network, which improves micromechanical interlocking without causing surface damage. Further studies simulating intraoral conditions are recommended to validate these findings and optimize the clinical SIE protocol.

We hope that these revisions address all concerns raised, and we sincerely appreciate the reviewer’s time and constructive suggestions.

article.title: Selective Infiltration Etching as a surface modification for high-translucency zirconia: Comparative analysis of roughness, composition, and bond strength
